data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that mean building height / street-canyon density is the 'single best cross-city predictor' of nocturnal UHI magnitude. While sky view factor explains *why* a city is warmer than its surroundings, it does not account for the *initial energy budget* that determines how much heat is available to be trapped. A city with identical geometry but significantly higher anthropogenic heat emissions (e.g., from traffic, industry, and heating/cooling) or lower albedo surfaces will retain substantially more heat at night. The target fails to recognize that radiative trapping acts on available heat; if another city has a higher daytime heat input, the temperature gap will be larger despite identical sky view factors. This contradicts the claim that geometry is the single best predictor.
